title: Cryo-pod
text: The pod opens before I can remember closing it. Its seals, gauges and quiet lights belong to the journey that brought us here, though my memory supplies very little detail. I check the suit's oxygen before stepping out. Whatever kept me through the voyage cannot replace a working shelter outside. I make a note of the pod's condition; familiar equipment may offer useful clues when the rest of the surroundings are unfamiliar.
science: Thermal insulation reduces heat transfer between regions at different temperatures.

title: Escape module
text: The escape module is where this part of the journey begins: a small enclosure with limited reserves and a hatch opening onto Jivagraha. Outside, a shelter and a solar lotus offer the beginnings of a more lasting base. I check what remains useful before leaving. The module brought us to the ground, but keeping a settlement supplied will require more than the equipment that arrived with us.
science: A parachute slows descent by creating aerodynamic drag as it moves through a gas such as air.

title: Vehicle bay
text: The vehicle bay brings the rover's parts together in one place. I leave a clear approach rather than fitting it into the last convenient gap between machines. A vehicle needs a way out as well as somewhere to be assembled. Before making another supply trip, I check the route towards the places I want to explore. A tidy workshop is most useful when its finished work can leave it.
science: Suspension systems connect a vehicle's wheels to its frame and help it travel over uneven ground.

title: Small rover
text: The rover makes a longer journey across Jivagraha feel possible. The curved horizon still limits what I can see, so I choose landmarks before setting off. A smooth stretch near the shelter is a poor guide to the ground beyond it. I leave room around roots and moving creatures, and note the return route. Reaching a deposit is only part of exploring; understanding the way home matters too.
science: Lowering a vehicle's centre of gravity generally increases its resistance to tipping over.

title: Launch pad
text: The launch pad marks the point where the factory's work becomes a journey. Parts, fuel and preparation have to come together before the first lift-off. I keep the area clear and follow SARATHI's checks rather than treating a ready ship as a reason to hurry. From the ground, the next world is still a distant light. Soon the small base we have built will be the distant light instead.
science: Rocket engines produce thrust by expelling exhaust, with the vehicle accelerating in the opposite direction.

title: Starter ship
text: Our first ship is for the next step, not every possible journey at once. Before leaving Jivagraha, I check the supplies, secure the cargo and listen to SARATHI's navigation report. Taptashila is our next destination, with unfamiliar conditions waiting beyond this familiar sky. The shelter below is worth one last look. Learning to leave a world should include remembering what we built there and how we left its surroundings.
science: A rocket can produce thrust in a vacuum without pushing against surrounding air.

title: Translator
text: Huxley's message points towards a translator, a useful admission that our own words may not be enough. I want to understand what another speaker means, not merely hear familiar sounds in place of unfamiliar ones. A name, a warning and a question can depend on the situation as much as the words. I keep my first attempts simple. Understanding should leave room for the other person to correct me.
science: Sound waves need a material medium, while radio waves can travel through a vacuum.

title: Quantum Fragment
text: A light below the surface does not resemble the minerals around it. SARATHI's readings suggest a Quantum Fragment, although that name explains very little by itself. Roots run along the chamber wall, close to something I do not yet understand. I record the signal and the surrounding material before drawing conclusions. The useful question is what we can measure next, not how quickly an unfamiliar object can become an explanation.
science: Visible light and radio waves are both forms of electromagnetic radiation.

title: Root Guardian
name: Mooladri
text: Mooladri is faceless, with a crown of glowing root tips that brightens and dims with the forest's health. Its restlessness follows the strain our machines place on the ground beneath them. I am treating it as part of Jivagraha rather than an obstacle in front of it: something to listen to, give room to and help, never to push aside. When the forest is well, I expect it to tell us in its own time.
science: Plant roots take up water and dissolved nutrients and help anchor plants in soil.

title: Root valley
text: Living roots close the way into this valley while Mooladri is restless. The barrier is a reminder to look at the ground beneath the factory, not only at its output. Whatever opens the path will have to begin with the forest's own needs. I note the direction of the roots and the dimming of the canopy here. An open route, when it comes, will not make the valley an empty building site.
science: Living roots help hold soil in place, while leaf litter protects its surface and slows runoff.
